name: Leonardo AI
description: Read-only Leonardo AI account surface: the API user's own details and token balances, the platform model catalogue, and one already-finished generation looked up by ID. NO GENERATION TOOL IS EXPOSED, deliberately: starting a Leonardo generation is a POST that spends API credits, so this connector carries no POST at all and cannot spend money.

tools.name: me
tools.description: Get the Leonardo AI user the API key belongs to, with current API and subscription token balances and concurrency slots

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List the Leonardo AI platform models available for generation, with id, name and description

tools.name: get_generation
tools.description: Get one existing Leonardo AI generation by ID: its status, prompt, dimensions, model and the URLs of the images it produced. Reads an existing generation only; it never starts one

generation_id.description: UUID of an existing Leonardo generation (e.g. 7f8a2b14-3c5d-4e6f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b)

needs_review: READ-ONLY BY DESIGN, AND FOR COST REASONS: no tool is marked write:true and no generation endpoint is present. Every Leonardo generation route (/generations, /generations-lcm, /generations-text-to-video, /generations-image-to-video, the variation and upscale routes) is a POST that consumes API credits on the same key, so exposing one would let an agent spend the customer's money. get_generation only LOOKS UP a generation that already exists.

base_url moved from the scaffolded 'https://cloud.leonardo.ai' (with full /api/rest/v1/... tool paths) to 'https://cloud.leonardo.ai/api/rest/v1' with relative paths. Same wire URL either way, but it changes the shape-proof CONTROL probe, and the difference was measured, not assumed: with a dummy bearer, https://cloud.leonardo.ai/<bogus> returns a Cloudflare 403 HTML page while /api/rest/v1/me returns a JSON 401, which the harness would have read as a path differential and scored SHAPE_PROVEN. Probing /api/rest/v1/<bogus> returns the byte-identical JSON 401 {error, path, code: access-denied} that every real path returns, so the honest class for this API is AUTH_WALL: host, TLS and auth rejection are proven, and the paths rest on the v1 OpenAPI document, not on this run.
auth kept as scaffolded (bearer api_key), confirmed against the live host: /me, /platformModels and an unrouted /api/rest/v1 path all answer a dummy bearer with the same structured JSON 401.

Response shapes taken from the v1.0 OpenAPI document (info.title 'Rest Endpoints', servers[0].url https://cloud.leonardo.ai/api/rest/v1) served by https://docs.leonardo.ai/v1.0/reference: /me returns {user_details: [...]}, /platformModels returns {custom_models: [...]} and /generations/{id} returns {generations_by_pk: {...}}. Leonardo also now publishes a v2 API (https://cloud.leonardo.ai/api/rest/v2); this spec is v1 only, which is what the vault entry's test endpoint targets.

get_generation carries a _probe hint so the shape-proof harness sends a syntactically valid v4 UUID (the path parameter is pattern-constrained), not the harness default 'quoxprobe'. It is a non-existent id, not a credential.
